title: USB Ethernet, cameras, and custom host drivers

spans.text: Plugging in a USB device is not enough: host software needs a driver for its USB class and enough memory and processing capacity.

USB flash drives need MSC plus a filesystem driver; wired networking needs a driver for the adapter's class (for example CDC-ECM/RNDIS); webcams need a USB Video Class (UVC) driver. Arduino-ESP32 TinyUSB host documents HID keyboard/mouse/gamepad, CDC serial, and MSC—this does not mean every Ethernet adapter or webcam works out of the box. Unsupported classes require a class driver using ESP-IDF USB Host or TinyUSB, including descriptors, endpoints, transfers, and class protocol.

Camera streams consume substantial RAM and bandwidth; a DVP camera board such as ESP32-CAM is often simpler. USB Ethernet needs driver and network-stack integration. Check VID/PID and class descriptors, then test a matching board and driver example before choosing hardware.

spans.title: Important safety and compatibility note
spans.text: Without a class driver, a USB Ethernet adapter or camera may enumerate but still provide no usable data. Verify S2/S3 host power, DMA/RAM budget, and network/camera support; the original ESP32 is not a USB host.
